model.name: Gazetteer Place
model.purpose: Governed context model for a gazetteer place: a named location instance recorded in a gazetteer or names register, including identifiers, toponyms, feature type, complementary position, hierarchy, name authority status, lifecycle, provenance, access constraints and interoperability alignments.
model.scope_statement: This model covers a Gazetteer Place as a real-world or historically attested geographic entity referred to by one or more proper names and recorded as a location instance in a gazetteer. A gazetteer is a register of location instances of one or more location classes that contains some information regarding position; that position need not be coordinates and may be descriptive. The model is format-neutral. It includes identity, linguistic name forms, classification, spatial reference by geographic identifier with optional complementary geometry, parent-child and associative relationships, officialization and historical status, record lifespan, source warrant, restricted disclosure, and crosswalk to peer gazetteers. Street addressing, coordinate reference-system definition, cadastral parcels, buildings as assets, transport networks, postal delivery zones and fictional places belong to sibling models.
in_scope: Named populated places, physical features, administrative named units and other named geographic entities as gazetteer location instances
Geographic identifiers, preferred and variant names, language, script, romanization, nativeness and name-status flags
Feature type or location class, including administrative versus physical characterisation
Complementary point, extent or footprint geometry and descriptive position
Hierarchical containment, polyhierarchy, disputed or historical parents, and associative links
Names-authority decisions, officialization, historical and lost places, merges and record lifespan
Source warrant, contributor, quality, restricted locations, licence and identifier concordance
out_of_scope: Street addresses, address components and postal addressing systems, which ISO 19112 assigns to ISO 19160-1
Definition of coordinate reference systems and datum operations, which belong to ISO 19111
Cadastral parcels, land tenure and property boundaries as primary objects
Buildings, structures, roads, airports and other cultural or constructed assets as primary objects
Transport networks as linear network topology
ZIP Codes and postal delivery areas
Fictional, legendary or purely imaginary places
Full GIS topology, elevation models, hydrographic sounding databases and cartographic product design

boundary_notes.distinction: A gazetteer place is a named location instance. An address is a structured spatial reference to a delivery or occupancy location that may mention a named place but is a different spatial-reference system. ISO 19112:2019 states that addressing is the subject of ISO 19160-1. INSPIRE Addresses may reference a NamedPlace; that reference is composition, not identity.

ISO 19112 spatial referencing uses geographic identifiers (labels or codes). Coordinates are complementary, not the primary key. Geometry and CRS definition stay in the coordinate sibling; this model only records a finding-purpose position or extent attached to the named place.

An administrative named place in a gazetteer identifies and classifies the named entity. Legal boundary geometry, jurisdiction and statistical units are sibling objects. INSPIRE NamedPlace.type and relatedSpatialObject point at other themes rather than embedding them. GNIS civil and census features are maintained by agreement and are not a substitute for boundary datasets.

Getty TGN records a built work as a place name only when the name functions as a place name; otherwise built works are out of TGN. USGS GNIS removed most cultural and man-made classes in 2021. Buildings as assets belong to a facility or built-work model.

A gazetteer is a georeferenced vocabulary of place-names, not a GIS. TGN coordinates are approximate finding aids. ISO 19112 positional information may be descriptive. Full geometry, topology and map portrayal are sibling concerns.

sources.title: ISO 19112:2019 Geographic information — Spatial referencing by geographic identifiers
sources.relevance: Normative conceptual schema for spatial referencing by geographic identifiers and for a gazetteer as a register of location instances. Distinguishes identifier-based referencing from ISO 19111 coordinates and treats addressing as ISO 19160-1.

sources.title: INSPIRE Data Specification on Geographical Names – Technical Guidelines
sources.organization: European Commission INSPIRE Maintenance and Implementation Group (MIG)
sources.version_or_date: Technical Guidelines published 2024-07-31 (theme Geographical Names; NamedPlace application schema)
sources.relevance: Authoritative European spatial-object model for NamedPlace and GeographicalName, including inspireId, geometry, type, related objects, lifespan, nativeness, nameStatus, spelling, language and viewing resolution.

sources.title: GeoNames Ontology
sources.relevance: Operational linked-data gazetteer feature model: geonamesID, Feature versus document URI, name and alternateName, featureClass/featureCode, parent hierarchy, nearby/neighbours/contains, WGS84 position, population, postalCode and licence metadata.

sources.title: Gazetteer Service – Application Profile of the Web Feature Service Best Practice (OGC 11-122r1)
sources.version_or_date: Version 1.0, published 2012-02-17 (OGC Best Practice, not an OGC Standard)
sources.relevance: Service and instance profile implementing ISO 19112 Location Instances: search and retrieve named places, gazetteer metadata, parent-child navigation and WFS transactions. Explicitly a Best Practice, not a conformance standard.

sources.title: Manual for the National Standardization of Geographical Names (UNGEGN, Statistical Papers Series M No. 88)
sources.organization: United Nations Group of Experts on Geographical Names / United Nations Statistics Division
sources.relevance: UN normative practice for national names authorities, standardized names versus allonyms, romanization, exonyms, indigenous names, gazetteer publication and the principle that a names authority sanctions the preferred name.

sources.title: About the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names (TGN)
sources.version_or_date: page as accessed 2026-08-24 (TGN reported 3,020,110 place records)
sources.relevance: Authoritative thesaurus model for a place record: Subject ID, names with flags, place types, polyhierarchy, associative relationships, approximate WGS 84 coordinates, sources, historical and lost places, merge mapping and explicit non-GIS stance.

sources.title: Domestic Names and the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)
sources.organization: U.S. Board on Geographic Names / U.S. Geological Survey
sources.version_or_date: page as accessed 2026-08-24; GNIS download cycle described as bi-monthly
sources.relevance: Federal names-authority process and national gazetteer for U.S. domestic names: Feature ID, official and variant names, feature class, historical flag, proposal and decision workflow, cave-location restriction, and explicit exclusions (roads, ZIP Codes, most cultural features).

sources.title: About GeoNames
sources.relevance: Documents GeoNames as a compiled gazetteer integrating NGA GNS, USGS GNIS and other national sources; nine feature classes and 645 feature codes; WGS84; Creative Commons Attribution licensing and wiki-style community update.

sources.title: ISO/TC 211 gazetteer schema requirement (ISO 19112:2019 /req/gaz/sch)
sources.relevance: Normative statement that gazetteer schema conformance is defined by ISO 19112:2019, grounding the Gazetteer object type as a first-class conformance target distinct from the spatial-reference-system class.

bundles.name: Identity and gazetteer register membership
bundles.description: How a gazetteer place is uniquely identified, how it is enrolled as a register item, and how external identifiers are concorded without treating a date as an identifier.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112:2019 treats a gazetteer as a register of location instances and a Location as a RegisterItem. INSPIRE, GNIS, GeoNames and TGN each issue a persistent master identifier. Concordance across those masters is an operating requirement, not optional metadata.

layers.name: Master identifiers and IRIs
layers.description: Authoritative system identifiers, governed IRIs and Dimension-assigned fallback identifiers for the place concept as distinct from any document about it.

findings.name: Authoritative master-system identifier
findings.description: Each gazetteer place must carry the identifier assigned by the authoritative names register or gazetteer that is master for the adopting context. GNIS Feature ID, INSPIRE inspireId, GeoNames geonamesID and TGN Subject ID are examples of persistent numeric or structured keys. A date is not an identifier. Merged or retired keys must be retained as former identifiers.

questions.text: What master-system identifier uniquely identifies this gazetteer place in the authoritative names register?
Which organisation and register is authoritative for this identifier in the adopting Dimension?
Which former, merged or superseded identifiers must still resolve to this place?
Is the identifier guaranteed stable across record versions, and under what merge or split events may it change?

data_elements.name: Master system identifier
data_elements.description: Persistent identifier assigned by the authoritative gazetteer or names register.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Scheme or namespace of the master identifier, for example GNIS Feature ID, inspireId, geonamesID or TGN Subject ID.

data_elements.name: Former identifiers
data_elements.description: Retired or merged identifiers that must continue to resolve to the surviving place.

artifacts.name: Identifier assignment record
artifacts.description: Governed record of the master identifier, issuing register, assignment event and any successor mapping after merge.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the issuing-register identifier; if the register later merges records, keep the surviving master id and map former ids.

findings.name: Governed IRI and identifier concordance
findings.description: Where a public IRI exists for the place concept, it is a governed global identifier distinct from the information resource about the place. GeoNames uses 303 redirection between the feature URI and the RDF document. TGN records NGA, USGS and Library of Congress identifiers to support concordance. A Dimension UUID or ULID is assigned only when no master or IRI exists.

questions.text: What governed IRI identifies the place concept as distinct from any document about it?
Which external gazetteer, thesaurus or authority identifiers are asserted as same-place concordances?
If no master-system identifier or governed IRI exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign?

data_elements.name: Concept IRI
data_elements.description: HTTP IRI identifying the place as a thing in the world, not the metadata document.

data_elements.name: Concordance identifiers
data_elements.description: Same-place identifiers in peer systems such as GNIS, NGA GNS, TGN, GeoNames or Library of Congress.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Fallback identifier minted by the adopting Dimension when no authoritative master id or IRI is available.

artifacts.name: Identifier concordance map
artifacts.description: Serial mapping of this place to peer-register identifiers with match method and confidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by master-system identifier with one row or triple per external scheme.

layers.name: Gazetteer as register
layers.description: Membership of the place in one or more gazetteers, including location class, custodian, territory of use and register item status.

findings.name: Gazetteer membership and register item
findings.description: ISO 19112:2019 defines a gazetteer as a register of location instances of one or more location sub-types containing some information regarding position, and recognises the gazetteer as a sub-type of ISO 19135-1 Register, with Location a RegisterItem. OGC WFS-G exposes gazetteer metadata and location instances over a feature service. A place may appear in more than one gazetteer.

questions.text: Which gazetteer or names register holds this location instance?
What is the register-item status of this location in that gazetteer?
Who is the custodian or overall owner of the gazetteer and of this location instance?
What is the territory of use and language or character-set scope of the gazetteer?

data_elements.name: Gazetteer identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the gazetteer register that contains this location instance.

data_elements.name: Register item status
data_elements.description: ISO 19135-style status of the location as a register item, such as valid, superseded or retired.

data_elements.name: Gazetteer custodian
data_elements.description: Responsible party that maintains the gazetteer.

data_elements.name: Territory of use
data_elements.description: Geographic extent within which the gazetteer or location class is intended to be used.

artifacts.name: Gazetteer location-instance record
artifacts.description: Canonical register item for the location instance, including gazetteer metadata, status and custodian.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of gazetteer identifier plus master location identifier.

findings.name: Location class in the identifier spatial reference system
findings.description: A spatial reference system using geographic identifiers is a collection of location classes; a gazetteer is a collection of location instances of one or more of those classes. The place must declare which location class or classes it instantiates.

questions.text: Which location class or classes does this place instantiate in the geographic-identifier spatial reference system?
Which spatial reference system using geographic identifiers governs this location class?
Who owns the location class definition and in which territory is it valid?

data_elements.name: Location class identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the LocationClass (ISO 19112:2019) or SI_LocationType (ISO 19112:2003 / OGC WFS-G) instantiated by this place.

data_elements.name: Location class definition
data_elements.description: Definition and identification rules for members of the class.

data_elements.name: Geographic-identifier SRS identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the SpatialReferenceSystemUsingGeographicIdentifiers that comprises the location class.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Location-class membership is typed reference data on the register item; it is not a separate serial artifact unless the Dimension publishes a location-class register extract.

bundles.name: Toponymy and linguistic form
bundles.description: The proper names by which the place is known, including spelling, language, script, romanization, nativeness, official status and sensitive or historical forms.
bundles.rationale: INSPIRE models one NamedPlace with many GeographicalName and SpellingOfName objects. UNGEGN distinguishes endonym and exonym and defines a standardized name as the form sanctioned by a names authority. TGN and GNIS retain variants, historical and deprecated forms for retrieval.

layers.name: Name set, spelling and conversion
layers.description: Preferred name, variants, language, script, transliteration or transcription scheme and pronunciation.

findings.name: Preferred name, variants and spellings
findings.description: A place has one or more proper names. INSPIRE requires at least one GeographicalName with at least one SpellingOfName.text. TGN flags a single record-preferred name and may flag a display name. UNGEGN defines a standardized name as the preferred name among allonyms. Homographs require parent context or a noted-homograph flag.

questions.text: What is the preferred or standardized name of this place for default display and indexing?
What variant, alternate, official, abbreviated or coded names are recorded for this place?
How is this name disambiguated from homographs, including parent string, qualifier or noted-homograph flag?
Does each name form have its own persistent term identifier distinct from the place identifier?

data_elements.name: Preferred name text
data_elements.description: Default preferred or standardized spelling of the place name.

data_elements.name: Name spellings
data_elements.description: Collection of written forms, each with script and optional transliteration scheme.

data_elements.name: Term identifier
data_elements.description: Persistent identifier of an individual name or term, distinct from the place subject identifier.

data_elements.name: Display name flag
data_elements.description: Whether this form should be used in horizontal labels to avoid confusion with a parent of the same name.

artifacts.name: Place name-set record
artifacts.description: Serial collection of preferred and variant names with flags, languages and term identifiers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by place master identifier plus term identifier or spelling hash.

findings.name: Language, script, romanization and pronunciation
findings.description: INSPIRE records language, ISO 15924 script and transliterationScheme on spellings, plus optional pronunciation. UNGEGN treats romanization keys as a distinct conversion from transcription and requires officially introduced romanization for non-Roman scripts. GeoNames stores language-tagged alternateName values.

questions.text: In which language or languages is each name form tagged, and which form is preferred per language?
What script is used for each spelling and which official romanization or transliteration scheme produced any converted form?
Is a pronunciation recorded for the name, and in what notation or audio evidence?

data_elements.name: Language code
data_elements.description: Language of the geographical name, typically ISO 639.

data_elements.name: Script code
data_elements.description: Writing system of the spelling, typically ISO 15924.

data_elements.name: Transliteration or romanization scheme
data_elements.description: Official conversion key used to produce a Roman or other converted spelling.

data_elements.name: Pronunciation
data_elements.description: Pronunciation of the name as text, IPA or linked audio.

artifacts.name: Romanization or pronunciation evidence
artifacts.description: Citation of the romanization key or pronunciation source applied to a spelling.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Cited by scheme identifier plus source URI; not a separate place identity.

layers.name: Nativeness, standardization and sensitive names
layers.description: Whether a name is an endonym or exonym, official or historical, and whether it is deprecated, pejorative or restricted for new indexing.

findings.name: Nativeness and name-status
findings.description: INSPIRE NativenessValue distinguishes endonym and exonym; NameStatusValue distinguishes official, standardised, historical and other, with Member State practice defining the precise meaning. UNGEGN definitions of endonym and exonym match INSPIRE. A names authority sanctions the standardized name among allonyms. INSPIRE does not itself rank competing official endonyms.

questions.text: Is each name an endonym, an exonym, or another nativeness category at the time of use?
What standardization or topicality status applies to each name, such as official, standardised, historical or other?
From which source or names authority was this name taken?

data_elements.name: Nativeness
data_elements.description: Endonym, exonym or other nativeness code for the name.

data_elements.name: Name status
data_elements.description: Credit given to the name with respect to standardisation and topicality.

data_elements.name: Source of name
data_elements.description: Origin from which the geographical name was taken.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Nativeness and name-status are coded attributes of each GeographicalName; they become artifacts only when a names-authority decision casefile is attached.

findings.name: Historical, deprecated and sensitive names
findings.description: TGN retains historical, misspelled, pejorative and avoid-use names for retrieval of legacy materials and flags them so they are not used for new indexing. GNIS marks obsolete names and vanished features as historical without implying age. GeoNames records historical and colloquial alternate-name types. These forms remain in the name set rather than being deleted.

questions.text: Which names are historical, local-use, misspellings or otherwise non-current, and for what period were they used?
Is any name flagged pejorative, deprecated or avoid-use, and may it still be used for retrieval of historical sources?
Are indigenous, minority or local-use names recorded, and under what community or authority warrant?

data_elements.name: Historical name flag
data_elements.description: Whether the name is current, historical, both, unknown or local-use.

data_elements.name: Sensitive or avoid-use flag
data_elements.description: Flags such as pejorative, deprecated, avoid-use or misspelling.

data_elements.name: Name use period
data_elements.description: Display date plus start and end years delimiting attested use of the name, not the existence of the place.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Sensitivity and historical flags are inline attributes of name forms. Deletion is not used; restriction of display is a policy overlay rather than a separate artifact.

bundles.name: Feature classification
bundles.description: The kind of geographic entity the name designates, including location class, named-place type, local type and administrative versus physical facet.
bundles.rationale: UNGEGN and INSPIRE treat feature type as a core gazetteer element. GeoNames, GNIS and TGN each publish incompatible type schemes that must be aligned rather than collapsed.

layers.name: Feature type and facet
layers.description: Typed characterisation of the named entity and the scheme that defines the codes.

findings.name: Feature type, location class and local type
findings.description: INSPIRE NamedPlace.type uses NamedPlaceTypeValue (administrativeUnit, populatedPlace, landform, hydrography, transportNetwork and others) and may add a data-provider localType. GeoNames uses nine feature classes and 645 feature codes. GNIS uses about 43 retrieval classes and states there are no official definitions for generic terms such as mountain versus hill. TGN place types are controlled terms linked to AAT. The type scheme in force must be declared; crosswalks are alignments, not identity.

questions.text: What feature type or named-place type is assigned, in which type scheme, and is a local type also recorded?
If a related spatial object in another theme is linked, is the feature type consistent with that theme?
What alignments exist between this type code and GeoNames, GNIS, TGN, INSPIRE or ADL feature-type concepts?

data_elements.name: Feature type code
data_elements.description: Code or concept identifying the kind of named entity in the declared type scheme.

data_elements.name: Type scheme
data_elements.description: Identifier of the feature-type thesaurus or code list in force.

data_elements.name: Local type
data_elements.description: Data-provider characterisation of the entity in at least one official language.

data_elements.name: GeoNames feature class and code
data_elements.description: Optional alignment to a GeoNames feature class and feature code.

artifacts.name: Feature-type scheme register extract
artifacts.description: The code list or thesaurus used to classify places, with definitions and history notes for deprecated codes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme IRI or register identifier plus version; codes are items in that register.

findings.name: Administrative versus physical facet
findings.description: TGN distinguishes Administrative records (inhabited places, nations, empires) from Physical records (mountains, rivers, oceans) and discourages a Both flag. Physical features that cross political boundaries are placed under the next containing hierarchical level. GNIS after 2021 focuses on natural features, unincorporated populated places and selected hydrographic and reservoir classes, and removed most cultural classes.

questions.text: Is this place classified as an administrative entity, a physical feature, or another facet used by the gazetteer?
Does a physical feature cross administrative boundaries, and under which containing parent is it placed?
If the gazetteer excludes cultural or constructed classes, is this entity in scope or must it be referenced in a sibling model?

data_elements.name: Record type or facet
data_elements.description: Administrative, physical, hierarchy guide term or other record-type flag.

data_elements.name: Crosses administrative boundary
data_elements.description: Whether the feature extends beyond a single administrative parent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Facet and boundary-crossing flags are classification attributes of the place record rather than independent artifacts.

bundles.name: Spatial reference and extent
bundles.description: How the place is spatially referenced by geographic identifier and, complementarily, by coordinates, extent, containment and cartographic viewing scale.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112 makes the geographic identifier the spatial reference and allows descriptive position. INSPIRE nevertheless requires geometry on NamedPlace. TGN and GeoNames use WGS 84 points as finding aids. These are complementary, not competing primary keys.

layers.name: Identifier reference, coordinates and geometry
layers.description: Geographic identifier as spatial reference, optional complementary coordinates, and optional footprint or bounding extent.

findings.name: Geographic identifier as spatial reference
findings.description: A geographic identifier is a spatial reference in the form of a label or code that identifies a location. ISO 19112 covers definition and recording of the referencing feature and does not model relative position to that feature. Positional information in a gazetteer need not be coordinates. Country names and similar labels are identifiers in this sense; postcodes are examples in ISO 19112 but addressing itself is out of this model's scope.

questions.text: What geographic identifier label or code is used as the spatial reference for this location?
If coordinates are absent, what descriptive spatial reference locates this place?
Within the location class and gazetteer, is the geographic identifier unique?

data_elements.name: Geographic identifier
data_elements.description: Label or code used as the spatial reference for the location.

data_elements.name: Alternative geographic identifiers
data_elements.description: Other labels or codes that also identify the location.

data_elements.name: Descriptive position
data_elements.description: Non-coordinate description of position, such as a containing named place or textual location.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The geographic identifier is the core inline spatial reference on the location instance; it is not a geometry artifact.

findings.name: Complementary coordinates and geometry
findings.description: ISO 19112 includes a mechanism for complementary coordinate references via ISO 19111. INSPIRE NamedPlace.geometry is mandatory and may be a point, curve, surface or bounding box; geometry types are otherwise unrestricted. GeoNames stores WGS84 lat/long. TGN stores approximate WGS 84 points (centre, or source for linear features), plus optional bounding coordinates and elevation, and states they are for finding purposes only. Coordinate observation time and ingestion time must be recorded separately when they differ.

questions.text: What complementary point position is recorded, in which CRS, and does it represent a centroid, mouth, source or other convention?
What geometry or geographic extent is associated with the named place, and at what precision or viewing resolution?
How approximate are the coordinates, from which source were they taken, and at what event time versus ingestion time?
Is elevation recorded, in what unit, and is it a measurement of the place or of a sampled point?

data_elements.name: Point position
data_elements.description: Complementary geographic point, typically WGS 84 latitude and longitude.

data_elements.name: Geographic extent
data_elements.description: Bounding box, footprint or other GM_Object associated with the named place.

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference system
data_elements.description: CRS of the complementary coordinates; WGS 84 is the de facto gazetteer finding CRS.

data_elements.name: Elevation
data_elements.description: Optional elevation of the place or sampled point.

data_elements.name: Coordinate event time
data_elements.description: Time the position was observed or originally published, distinct from ingestion time.

artifacts.name: Place geometry representation
artifacts.description: Serial geometry or extent for the named place, including CRS, role and quality statement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Attached to the place master identifier with a geometry-role and CRS; not used as the place identifier.

layers.name: Containment, territory and viewing scale
layers.description: Administrative or physical containment used as context, plus cartographic scale guidance.

findings.name: Containment context and viewing resolution
findings.description: GNIS locates a feature by State, county, topographic map and coordinates. GeoNames records countryCode and parentADM1–ADM4. INSPIRE may record leastDetailedViewingResolution and mostDetailedViewingResolution so names are not shown at inappropriate scales. Census Gazetteer files list codes, names, area and representative coordinates for statistical geographies; those files are a sibling statistical gazetteer, not the names-authority record.

questions.text: In which country and administrative units is this place located for gazetteer context, without treating those units as this place?
On which map sheet or topographic map is the place located, if the gazetteer uses map references?
At which least and most detailed viewing resolutions should the named place be displayed?

data_elements.name: Country code
data_elements.description: ISO country code of the containing country when applicable.

data_elements.name: Administrative context
data_elements.description: Containing administrative units used as gazetteer context.

data_elements.name: Viewing resolution
data_elements.description: Indicative scale or ground distance bounds for display of the name.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Administrative context and viewing resolution are attributes of the place or of a cartographic portrayal rule, not independent place artifacts.

bundles.name: Relationships and related objects
bundles.description: Hierarchical whole/part structure, polyhierarchy including historical and disputed parents, and associative, nearby, neighbour and related-spatial-object links.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19112 and OGC WFS-G model parent and child location instances. TGN is polyhierarchical and adds associative thesaurus relations. GeoNames exposes contains, neighbours and nearby. INSPIRE relatedPlace and relatedSpatialObject preserve consistency across themes and levels of detail.

layers.name: Hierarchy and associative links
layers.description: Parent-child structure and non-hierarchical relations to other places or spatial objects.

findings.name: Parent-child hierarchy and polyhierarchy
findings.description: Location instances nest through parent and child associations. TGN uses whole/part (partitive) relations, allows multiple parents with one preferred, flags current versus historical parent links, and dates those links. Unusual cases include cities in two counties, disputed sovereignty and physical features under the next fully containing parent. OGC WFS-G requires the service to fetch and follow parent-child links.

questions.text: What is the preferred parent place, and what whole/part or other hierarchical relation type applies?
What additional current, historical or disputed parents exist, and over which time span?
Which child places are contained, and in what sort order should siblings be listed?

data_elements.name: Parent links
data_elements.description: Links to broader location instances with relation type, preferred flag and optional dates.

data_elements.name: Child links
data_elements.description: Links to narrower location instances.

data_elements.name: Hierarchy relation type
data_elements.description: Whole/part, genus/species or instance relation as used by the gazetteer.

artifacts.name: Hierarchy path record
artifacts.description: Materialised preferred and alternate ancestor paths used for labels and retrieval.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived from place id plus parent-link set; rebuild on parent change.

findings.name: Associative, nearby and related spatial objects
findings.description: TGN associative relations include distinguished from, ally of, capital of and successor of. GeoNames provides neighbours for countries and nearby features. INSPIRE relatedPlace links other NamedPlace instances; relatedSpatialObject points at the same real-world entity in another INSPIRE theme when that object has an identifier. These links must not silently collapse distinct real-world entities.

questions.text: What associative relations to other gazetteer places are recorded, with which controlled relation type?
Which neighbouring or nearby features are asserted, and is the relation topological, proximity-based or both?
Which identifiers of spatial objects in other themes represent the same entity as this named place?

data_elements.name: Associative links
data_elements.description: Non-hierarchical relations to other place records.

data_elements.name: Nearby or neighbour links
data_elements.description: Proximity or adjacency relations exposed by the gazetteer.

data_elements.name: Related spatial objects
data_elements.description: Identifiers of same-entity objects in other spatial data themes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Associative and related-object links are typed references on the place record. They become artifacts only when exported as a linkset.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, names authority and time
bundles.description: Officialization and proposal processes, existence of the feature, historical and lost places, merges, and the distinction between real-world time and record lifespan.
bundles.rationale: BGN and UNGEGN treat name standardization as an authority process, not a wiki edit. INSPIRE lifespan attributes timestamp the spatial-object version, not the feature's existence. TGN and GNIS keep vanished and renamed places.

layers.name: Names authority, officialization and existence
layers.description: Who may sanction a name, how proposals are decided, and whether the feature still exists.

findings.name: Names authority, proposal and officialization
findings.description: UNGEGN defines a standardized name as a name sanctioned by a names authority as the preferred name among allonyms and documents an owner-decides principle in some national practice. The U.S. BGN Domestic Names Committee decides proposals for new names and name changes under published Principles, Policies and Procedures; compelling reason is required to change an existing name. Community wiki edits in GeoNames are not equivalent to names-authority sanction.

questions.text: Which names authority has jurisdiction to sanction or change the official name of this feature, and in which territory?
What is the current officialization state of the name, including any pending proposal or BGN-equivalent decision date?
What local usage, historical warrant and compelling reason support a proposed new name or name change?
Does a landowner, indigenous community or other owner-decides rule constrain who may propose or approve the name?

data_elements.name: Names authority
data_elements.description: Organisation empowered to sanction standardized names for this territory and feature class.

data_elements.name: Decision status
data_elements.description: Official, proposed, rejected, deferred or not-decided status of the name.

data_elements.name: Proposal identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a names-proposal case before the names authority.

artifacts.name: Name decision casefile
artifacts.description: Proposal, evidence, meeting action and decision for officialization or change of a geographic name.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Proposal or decision identifier assigned by the names authority; linked to the place master identifier.

findings.name: Existence, historical, lost and merged places
findings.description: GNIS marks features that no longer exist, or names no longer used, as historical, without implying age or condition. TGN includes lost settlements that have historical warrant, planned-but-unbuilt settlements, and archaeological sites, and excludes legendary places. Merged TGN records provide former-key mappings. GeoNames includes historical feature codes. These states are lifecycle of the named entity, not merely of the database row.

questions.text: Does the named feature still exist on the landscape, is it historical, lost, planned-unbuilt, or merged into another place?
If the precise location is unknown or the place is lost, what historical warrant still justifies a gazetteer record?
If records were merged or split, which surviving identifier is canonical and which former identifiers redirect?

data_elements.name: Existence state
data_elements.description: Extant, historical, lost, planned-unbuilt, merged or unknown.

data_elements.name: Location certainty
data_elements.description: Whether the location is known, approximate or unknown for a historically attested place.

data_elements.name: Successor place identifier
data_elements.description: Place that succeeds this one after rename, merge or political succession.

artifacts.name: Merge and split map
artifacts.description: Mapping of defunct place identifiers to surviving records after merge or split.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each former identifier maps to exactly one current master identifier at a given time.

layers.name: Validity periods and record lifespan
layers.description: Real-world time for names, types and relations versus database version lifespan.

findings.name: Real-world validity versus record lifespan
findings.description: INSPIRE beginLifespanVersion and endLifespanVersion timestamp insertion or retirement of a spatial-object version in the dataset and are distinct from the temporal characteristics of the real-world entity. TGN uses display dates plus start and end years in the proleptic Gregorian calendar, with BCE as negative years and 9999 for still-current. GeoNames records dcterms:created and dcterms:modified on the document, and a modification date on dump records. Event time and ingestion time must both be stored when they differ, in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

questions.text: What real-world interval applies to the place type, name use or parent relation, as distinct from database version time?
When was this version of the spatial object inserted, superseded or retired in the gazetteer dataset?
What is the event time of the underlying naming or geometry fact versus the observation or ingestion time of this record?

data_elements.name: Real-world valid from
data_elements.description: Start of real-world applicability for a name, type or relation.

data_elements.name: Real-world valid to
data_elements.description: End of real-world applicability; open if still current.

data_elements.name: Begin lifespan version
data_elements.description: Date-time this version was inserted or changed in the dataset.

data_elements.name: End lifespan version
data_elements.description: Date-time this version was superseded or retired in the dataset.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Time the adopting Dimension observed or ingested the fact.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal fields are inline on names, relations and register versions. Serial artifacts are the versioned place record itself, not a separate time object.

bundles.name: Evidence, access, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: Source warrant, quality, restricted disclosure, licence, retention of historical names, and service or encoding interoperability.
bundles.rationale: TGN requires cited sources for names and notes. GNIS withholds cave locations under U.S. cave-protection law. GeoNames is CC BY. OGC WFS-G defines query and transaction operations. These are operating constraints, not optional annotations.

layers.name: Source warrant and quality
layers.description: Citations, contributors, homograph handling and coordinate quality.

findings.name: Source warrant, contributor and quality
findings.description: TGN requires a controlled source citation and page or record locator for each name, and cites sources for descriptive notes. Contributors are recorded per name and note. GeoNames compiles NGA, GNIS, Ordnance Survey and other sources and allows wiki correction under licence. Homographs, approximate coordinates and compiled-versus-authority origin are quality dimensions. Population figures in GeoNames are optional measurements, not names-authority facts.

questions.text: What published or archival source warrants each name, and where in that source was it found?
Which institution or project contributed each name, note or geometry, and is that form the contributor preferred form?
What quality or confidence applies to the identifier match, coordinates and feature type, and is the record compiled or authority-sanctioned?
If population or similar measurements are present, are they gazetteer finding aids or references to a demographic sibling?

data_elements.name: Source citations
data_elements.description: Bibliographic or database citations warranting names, notes or coordinates.

data_elements.name: Contributor
data_elements.description: Institution or project that contributed a name or note.

data_elements.name: Quality flags
data_elements.description: Confidence, coordinate approximation and authority-sanctioned versus compiled origin.

data_elements.name: Population
data_elements.description: Optional population finding aid; not a substitute for a census dataset.

artifacts.name: Source citation record
artifacts.description: Reusable bibliographic or database citation used as warrant for names and notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Citation identifier in a source register; page or external record id stored on the link to the name.

layers.name: Restricted locations, licence and retention
layers.description: Disclosure exceptions, licence terms and the rule that historical and sensitive names are retained rather than deleted.

findings.name: Restricted disclosure, licence and retention
findings.description: GNIS includes caves but does not publicly release cave locations, citing the Federal Cave Resources Protection Act and 43 CFR Part 37. Historical names and vanished features are retained and flagged, not deleted. TGN keeps pejorative and avoid-use names for retrieval of historical materials. GeoNames data is licensed Creative Commons Attribution. Compiled gazetteers must not present community edits as names-authority decisions.

questions.text: Is location or even existence of this feature publicly disclosable, or is it withheld under cave-protection or other sensitivity law?
Under what licence may the gazetteer record and its names be reused, and what attribution is required?
May historical, pejorative or superseded names be deleted, or must they be retained with flags for retrieval and audit?
What exception process grants an agent access to redacted coordinates or suppressed names?

data_elements.name: Disclosure code
data_elements.description: Public, restricted, coordinates-withheld or existence-withheld.

data_elements.name: Licence URI
data_elements.description: Licence under which the record may be reused.

data_elements.name: Retention rule
data_elements.description: Whether historical and sensitive names are retained, flagged or eligible for deletion.

artifacts.name: Access exception record
artifacts.description: Auditable grant of access to withheld location or suppressed name.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Exception identifier plus agent and time; never use the withheld coordinates as the record key.

layers.name: Crosswalk, encoding and services
layers.description: How gazetteer places are queried, transacted and mapped across encodings without treating JSON, GML, RDF or a database as the semantics.

findings.name: Crosswalk, services and exchange
findings.description: OGC 11-122r1 profiles WFS so clients can discover a gazetteer, query location instances by name without inspecting feature-type internals, read gazetteer metadata, follow parent-child links and apply insert, update and delete transactions. It remains a Best Practice, not an OGC Standard; OGC API Features is the modern successor interface family. INSPIRE Geographical Names is an encoding of NamedPlace, not the only encoding. GeoNames exposes search, RDF and dump projections of the same Feature. UNGEGN Resolution 4 of the first UN Conference listed geographic name, feature type and location as the minimum digital-exchange set.

questions.text: Through which gazetteer service operations can an agent resolve, search, insert, update or delete this location instance?
Does an exported record include the UNGEGN minimum of standardized name, feature type and location, plus any required INSPIRE or ISO fields?
Which encodings are projections of this place rather than alternative semantics, and how is round-trip identity preserved?
Is any conformance claimed to ISO 19112, INSPIRE GN or OGC WFS-G, and what evidence supports the claim?

data_elements.name: Service profile
data_elements.description: Declared query or transaction profile such as OGC WFS-G or a successor API.

data_elements.name: Supported operations
data_elements.description: Discovery, query and transaction operations offered for gazetteer items.

data_elements.name: Conformance target
data_elements.description: Standard or profile against which interoperability is claimed, with evidence pointer.

artifacts.name: Gazetteer exchange record
artifacts.description: Encoding-neutral payload projected to GML, RDF, dump or API feature while preserving master identity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier remains the identity in every projection; encoding format is not an identifier.

functions.name: Resolve place by identifier
functions.description: Return the gazetteer location instance that matches a master-system identifier, governed IRI, concordance key or former identifier.
outputs: redirect from former identifier if merged
preconditions: Agent is authorised for the disclosure class of the record
effects: No state change unless an audit of the resolution is required for restricted records

functions.name: Search places by name
functions.description: Query location instances by preferred or variant name, with optional language, feature type, bounding box and gazetteer scope, including homograph disambiguation via parent context.
preconditions: Search scope is within the agent's access policy
effects: Returns matching location instances without mutating them

functions.name: Geocode name to complementary position
functions.description: Map a geographic identifier or name to complementary coordinates or descriptive position. This is gazetteer lookup, not address geocoding.
effects: Returns complementary position; does not mint a new place

functions.name: Reverse geocode position to candidate places
functions.description: Return named places whose position or extent contains or is near a point, filtered by feature type and viewing resolution.
preconditions: Point CRS is known or assumed WGS 84 as a finding CRS
effects: Read-only candidate set; proximity is not a hierarchical parent

functions.name: Traverse parent-child hierarchy
functions.description: Follow preferred and additional parents or children, including historical and polyhierarchical paths.

functions.name: Propose a new name or name change
functions.description: Submit a names-authority proposal for an unnamed feature or a change to an existing official name, with local-usage evidence and compelling reason.
preconditions: Proposer meets the names-authority submission rules
Feature class is within the authority's purview
effects: Creates a proposal casefile; does not by itself change the standardized name

functions.name: Decide official name
functions.description: Record a names-authority decision that sanctions, rejects or defers a standardized name.
effects: Updates standardized name and name-status; retains prior names as historical or variant

functions.name: Merge or split place records
functions.description: Collapse duplicate location instances or split a conflated record, preserving former-identifier redirects.
preconditions: Sources cited for sameness or distinctness
effects: One surviving master identifier; absorbed identifiers become former identifiers

functions.name: Restrict or redact sensitive location
functions.description: Withhold coordinates or public existence of features such as caves, while retaining the governed record for authorised agents.
preconditions: Legal or policy basis for restriction exists
effects: Public projections omit withheld geometry; audit log records authorised access

functions.name: Publish or transact a gazetteer item
functions.description: Insert, update or retire a location instance through a gazetteer service or register process, including ISO 19135-style item status.
preconditions: Record satisfies the gazetteer schema and validation policies
effects: Creates or versions the register item; sets lifespan timestamps; may emit exchange encodings

composition.purpose: Align the Gazetteer Place entity to ISO 19112 Location as a register item in a Gazetteer, with GeographicIdentifier as the spatial reference and complementary coordinates via ISO 19111.

ISO 19112:2019 treats Gazetteer as a Register, LocationClass as ItemClass and Location as RegisterItem; mix in register-item identity, status and management without duplicating a generic register model.
Align names, geometry, type, related objects and lifespan fields to the INSPIRE NamedPlace / GeographicalName application schema for European exchange.
Align query, metadata and parent-child operations to the OGC gazetteer service profile while recording that it is a Best Practice, not an OGC Standard.
Optional concordance and type-code alignment to GeoNames Feature, including concept-versus-document IRIs.
Optional alignment for historical, multilingual and polyhierarchical place records, including associative relations and source citations.
Reference CRS definition for complementary coordinates; do not embed CRS semantics in the gazetteer place.
Addresses may mention or locate within a named place; addressing is a sibling spatial-reference system, not a gazetteer place.
Containing administrative units provide context and possible relatedSpatialObject links; legal boundaries remain a sibling.
Constructed works are referenced only when a building name functions as a place name; otherwise they are out of gazetteer-place scope.
Mix in dataset-level and responsible-party metadata for gazetteer custodianship, lineage and constraints without making metadata the place.

owner_package_requirements: Designate the names authority versus the gazetteer operator and the territory of use for which the Dimension is master.
Declare the identifier policy: which external register is master, when a Dimension UUID may be minted, and how former identifiers redirect.
Declare the feature-type scheme in force and any required crosswalks to INSPIRE, GeoNames, GNIS or TGN.
Declare geometry policy: whether complementary coordinates are mandatory, which CRS is the finding CRS, and how approximate coordinates are flagged.
Declare disclosure, indigenous-name and historical-name retention policies, including cave or other withheld-location rules.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Prefer the authoritative names-register identifier as the business key. If a public concept IRI exists, store it as a governed global identifier distinct from any document URI. Mint a Dimension UUID or ULID only when neither is available. Do not use a date, coordinates or a preferred-name string as the identifier. Namespace local IRIs under the Dimension's registry namespace and record the issuing register on every imported id.
registry_links: USGS GNIS / U.S. Board on Geographic Names (https://www.usgs.gov/us-board-on-geographic-names/domestic-names)

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity is the master-system identifier in the declared issuing register, then a governed concept IRI, then a Dimension UUID or ULID.
The preferred or standardized name is a display property, never the identity; compare names only after language, script and romanization are declared.
Complementary WGS 84 points used as finding aids must not be rounded into identity; preserve source precision and role (centroid, mouth, source).
Parent paths used in labels are derived; the stored facts are individual parent links with preferred and historical flags.
Encodings (JSON, GML, RDF, CSV dumps, MongoDB documents) are projections of the same location instance.
patch_rules: Name-set patches add or flag variants; they do not delete historical, pejorative or avoid-use names except under an explicit retention exception.
Official-name changes require a names-authority decision artifact; a wiki or crowd edit cannot silently overwrite a sanctioned name.
Merge patches must write former-identifier mappings before retiring an absorbed record.
Geometry patches record event time and ingestion time separately and must not replace withheld coordinates in the public projection.
Feature-type patches must declare the type scheme and, if relatedSpatialObject is set, remain consistent with that theme.
compatibility_rules: ISO 19112:2003 SI_LocationInstance property names used by OGC 11-122r1 must map to ISO 19112:2019 Location / GeographicIdentifier without claiming identical UML.

INSPIRE geometry cardinality (required) is stricter than ISO 19112 (position optional and possibly descriptive); importers must not drop places that lack coordinates unless the Dimension requires geometry.
OGC 11-122r1 is a Best Practice; do not advertise OGC Standard conformance on that basis.
GeoNames community updates are compiled data; they do not replace BGN, UNGEGN national authority or INSPIRE member-state official names.
Feature-type codes are not interchangeable across GeoNames, GNIS, TGN and INSPIRE without an explicit crosswalk.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the names register or national gazetteer that is master for the territory (for example GNIS Feature ID, INSPIRE inspireId, national gazetteer id).
Governed global identifier or concept IRI when published (for example GeoNames sws URI or TGN LOD URI), distinct from the information-resource URI.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension only when no master identifier or governed IRI exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record real-world event time (name use, decision, geometry observation) separately from observation or ingestion time and from dataset beginLifespanVersion / endLifespanVersion.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named {place-master-id}-{artifact-type}-v{n} or, for authority casefiles, {proposal-id}-v{n}. Encoding suffixes are not part of identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every serial artifact carries the place master identifier, a content checksum or equivalent integrity stamp, provenance of the last patch, and a disclosure class. Public projections of restricted records must not leak withheld coordinates.

policies: Standardized or official names take display precedence over compiled or crowd-sourced forms when a names authority has jurisdiction.
Historical, variant, pejorative and avoid-use names are retained with flags for retrieval and audit; they are not used for new indexing.
Indigenous, minority and local-use names are recorded with community or authority warrant and are not overwritten by exonyms.
Cave and other legally protected locations have coordinates withheld from public projections.
Addresses, postal codes, buildings-as-assets and CRS definitions are referenced, not stored as the gazetteer place.
Conformance to ISO 19112, INSPIRE GN or OGC WFS-G is claimed only with evidence; otherwise records are alignments.

read: Any authorised agent may resolve and search public gazetteer places within declared viewing and disclosure rules.
Restricted coordinates and suppressed names are readable only by roles listed on an access exception.
Parent-child, concordance and source citations are readable with the place unless separately classified.
create: Gazetteer custodians may insert location instances that meet identifier, name, type-scheme and disclosure policies.
Names-authority proposals create casefiles; they do not create official names until decided.
Crowd or compiled imports must be flagged as compiled and cannot mint official status.
update: Editors may add variants, concordance, geometry quality and hierarchy links.
Official-name and existence-state changes require names-authority or custodian role as declared.
Lifespan timestamps are system-set on version change and are not user-editable event times.
delete: Hard delete of an official or historical place is forbidden; retire via register-item status and endLifespanVersion.
Absorbed records are merged, not deleted, with former-identifier maps retained.
Only Dimension-assigned draft UUIDs with no authority sanction may be physically removed before first publication.

roles.name: Names authority
responsibilities: Sanction standardized names and decide proposals for the declared territory and feature classes
Set official versus historical name status
Remain distinct from the technical gazetteer operator

roles.name: Gazetteer custodian
responsibilities: Operate the gazetteer register, identifier assignment and exchange services
Maintain location-class definitions, territory of use and dataset lifespan
Publish AGENTS.md, schema and process URLs

roles.name: Toponymic editor
responsibilities: Add variant names, sources, hierarchy links and quality flags
Prepare merge and split proposals with warrant
Must not silently override names-authority decisions

roles.name: Sensitivity officer
responsibilities: Classify disclosure of caves and other withheld locations
Approve access exceptions and review public projections for leakage

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Resolve, search and geocode within access policy
Record ingestion time separately from source event time

access.default_rule: Public read of non-restricted gazetteer places and names; write restricted to custodian, editor and names-authority roles; withheld coordinates default to deny.
exceptions: Authorised researchers or land-management agents may receive withheld cave or other protected coordinates under an auditable exception.
Indigenous-name records may have community-specified access tighter than the gazetteer default.
Internal compiled dumps may include licence-restricted sources that cannot be redistributed.
audit_requirements: Log identifier resolution of restricted records, all official-name decisions, merges, disclosure-class changes and access exceptions with RFC 3339 timestamps and actor identity.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the Specification URL for the Gazetteer Place context model and identifier policy.
Read the Storage type URL for the projection in use; do not treat storage format as semantics.
Read the Interface URL for resolve, search and transaction operations.
Read the Processes URL for names-authority, merge, restriction and publication procedures.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the defensible operating surface of a Gazetteer Place as a named location instance: identity, toponymy, feature type, identifier-based spatial reference with complementary geometry, hierarchy, names-authority lifecycle, provenance, restricted disclosure and interoperability alignments to ISO 19112, INSPIRE Geographical Names, OGC WFS-G, UNGEGN practice, GNIS and major compiled gazetteers. It does not claim a single global feature-type scheme, a universal official-name authority, or completeness for marine, extraterrestrial or historical-linked-places ecosystems.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifiers, concept IRIs, concordance and Dimension UUID fallback; dates excluded as identifiers.
Officialization, existence, historical and lost places, merge or split, register-item status and dataset lifespan.
Parent-child, polyhierarchy, associative, nearby, neighbour and relatedSpatialObject links.
Real-world name and relation intervals versus begin/end lifespan versus ingestion time, RFC 3339.
Source citations, contributors, compiled versus authority-sanctioned origin.
Gazetteer custodian, location administrator, names authority and owner-decides constraints.
Identifier uniqueness in class, type consistency with related objects, minimum exchange set, conformance evidence.
Public versus restricted disclosure, licence, exception grants and role scopes.
Historical and sensitive names retained and flagged; hard delete forbidden for published official records.
Alignments to ISO 19112, INSPIRE GN, OGC WFS-G, GeoNames and TGN; encodings treated as projections.
Preferred and variant names, language, script, romanization, nativeness, name-status and sensitive-name flags.
Geographic identifier as spatial reference, complementary WGS 84 points, extent, containment context and viewing resolution.
Location class, named-place type, local type and administrative versus physical facet, with crosswalk as alignment.
UNGEGN standardized-name concept and BGN proposal/decision process; wiki edits are not sanction.
Cave-location withholding and pejorative or avoid-use name handling.

known_omissions: Full ISO 19112:2019 UML attribute list is paywalled; 2019 class names (Location, LocationClass, Gazetteer, GeographicIdentifier) are taken from the official abstract, TC 211 requirement and publicly quoted edition-2 change list, while 2003 SI_* properties are evidenced by OGC 11-122r1.
NGA GNS field dictionary (UFI/UNI, name type, designation) was not retrieved; non-US official names often depend on that register and remain a gap.
IHO SCUFN undersea feature names, IAU WGPSN extraterrestrial names, and World Historical Gazetteer / Linked Places Format / Pelagios are not primary-sourced here.
Indigenous data-sovereignty protocols (CARE Principles, UNDRIP applied to toponyms) are only indirectly covered via UNGEGN promotion of indigenous names.
ADL Gazetteer Content Standard and Feature Type Thesaurus are historically important but were not fetched as live first-party schema in this run.
ISO 19155 Place Identifier architecture and GeoSPARQL geometry semantics are not modelled beyond complementary geometry.
National gazetteers beyond GNIS/INSPIRE/GeoNames/TGN (for example Ordnance Survey Open Names, Canadian Geographical Names) are acknowledged as sources to GeoNames rather than fully modelled.
conflicts: ISO 19112:2019 optional/descriptive position versus INSPIRE NamedPlace required geometry.
ISO 19112:2019 Location/Gazetteer class names versus OGC 11-122r1 use of ISO 19112:2003 SI_LocationInstance.
OGC 11-122r1 is a Best Practice, not an OGC Standard; OGC now points implementers to OGC API Features.
Feature-type schemes conflict: INSPIRE NamedPlaceTypeValue, GeoNames 9 classes/645 codes, GNIS ~43 retrieval classes with no official generic-term definitions, TGN AAT-linked place types.
GNIS 2021 removal of most cultural feature classes versus GeoNames and TGN retention of many man-made or inhabited-place types.
GeoNames wiki edits versus UNGEGN/BGN names-authority sanction.
TGN approximate finding coordinates versus GIS-grade geometry.
INSPIRE does not rank competing official endonyms; UNGEGN prefers a single official spelling per feature where possible.
regional_assumptions: WGS 84 is assumed as the de facto finding CRS for complementary points (GeoNames, TGN, typical GNIS decimal degrees), not as a universal legal CRS.
U.S. BGN/GNIS rules, including cave-location withholding and cultural-feature exclusions, apply to U.S. domestic names and must not be globalised.
INSPIRE NamedPlace obligations apply to European spatial-data infrastructure exchange, not to all gazetteers.
UNGEGN romanization keys and endonym preference apply where a national names authority exists; many territories have none.
English-language preferred-name practice in TGN legacy data is an editorial convention, not a global rule.
NGA GNS remains the usual non-US official compiled source even though its field dictionary was not fetched.
adversarial_checks: Could an address, postal code or cadastral parcel be smuggled in as a gazetteer place? ISO 19112 sends addressing to ISO 19160-1; GNIS explicitly excludes ZIP Codes; those remain sibling models.
Could a date, centroid or preferred-name string be used as identity? The identity priority forbids it; merges require former-id maps rather than renaming the key to a date.
Could community GeoNames edits be treated as BGN or UNGEGN official names? Policy requires authority-sanctioned versus compiled flags.
Could withheld cave coordinates leak through nearby, dump or reverse-geocode functions? Restrict-sensitive-location and access exceptions exist specifically to prevent that.

Could ISO 19112:2019 conformance be claimed from OGC 11-122r1 or from INSPIRE GN alone? Conflicts and Best Practice status are recorded; conformance requires evidence against the 2019 gazetteer conformance class.
Could fictional or legendary places enter via historical-lost handling? TGN excludes legendary places; location-certainty and historical warrant questions force that distinction.
Could feature-type crosswalks silently equate mountain, peak and populated place across schemes? Type scheme is mandatory and crosswalk is an alignment with mapping notes.
